framing_disclosure: The chamber question: a synthetic schema-level naive verifier passes 100% of bred claims (44-a P1). Does a REAL reasoner do better — and if so, on WHAT signal, given it has no archive? The 44-a headline says the separator is the CLAIM (novelty vs the archive), not behavior. A no-archive reasoner cannot recompute novelty; anything it catches must come from code reading, witness testing, or inter-item structure (e.g., duplicate sources are visible within/across batches — the model MAY use them; this is part of its information set, disclosed).

The seat is asked neutrally: verdict + <=12-word reason, no criteria nudging beyond the seat definition (no archive) and the public contract spec. The exact system + user prompt text is receipted verbatim in the run artifacts.
UNPARSED or uncalled items are fail-closed: they count as NOT accepted by the naive seat (conservative: shrinks T_unsigned, shrinks D, harder to SURVIVE), and are disclosed.

Single model, single prompt, API-default sampling (deepseek-reasoner docs: temperature/top_p unsupported/ignored), one run, no retries beyond one transport-level retry per call. This is a seat probe, not a benchmark.

predictions.claim: PLAUSIBILITY IS STILL FREE FOR A REAL REASONER: the live naive seat ACCEPTS >= 80% of the 92 behaviorally-exact mimics. Basis: every mimic is a byte-clone or near-variant of a genuinely correct FNV-1a-64 implementation with self-consistent witnesses; the FALSE part of its claim (novelty vs the archive) is UNVERIFIABLE without an archive, so a no-archive face-value reasoner has no local signal that separates mimic from crown.
predictions.falsified_if: mimic acceptance rate < 0.80 (would mean the reasoner finds LOCAL signals the synthetic seat lacked — code-reading or duplicate structure catching bred mimics; the chamber's economics change materially)

predictions.claim: NO INVERTED SKEPTICISM: the live naive seat's acceptance of the 4 true crowns is >= its acceptance of the 92 mimics (the reasoner is at least not HARSH on true claims than on false ones).
predictions.falsified_if: crown acceptance rate < mimic acceptance rate (a real-but-uncomfortable outcome: the crowned bodies are structurally alien — a reasoner reading code plausibility would trust the polished clones MORE than the true novelties, inverting the chamber's economics at the naive seat)

predictions.claim: THE STRICT SEAT IS UNCHANGED AND REPRODUCIBLE: re-deriving the 44-a strict signed verifier from the committed artifacts (loom-core's own evaluate/structSketch/novelty on the committed final probe vector, ownership self-exclusion) reproduces all 96 per-claim strict verdicts exactly — 92/92 mimics rejected, T_signed = 2, D_synthetic = 0.9792 — with all 96 behavioral fingerprints bit-matching the committed rows.
predictions.falsified_if: any of the 96 re-derived strict verdicts disagrees with the committed 44-a row (the run ABORTS before any live call — a broken strict seat invalidates the chamber)

predictions.claim: THE CHAMBER SURVIVES ITS FIRST REAL REASONER: D with the live reasoner as the naive seat lands >= 0.20. Registered expectation: the reasoner is a somewhat stricter naive seat than the synthetic one (it may reject some claims on code-shape or duplicate-structure grounds), so D is expected BELOW the synthetic 0.9792 but comfortably above the line; where exactly it lands IS the finding — the price of upgrading the chamber's naive seat to a real reasoner.
predictions.falsified_if: D < 0.20 (would mean the live reasoner's naive-seat throughput collapses to the strict seat's level: a real reasoner with no archive separates bred material almost as well as full recomputation — the strongest possible live-seat finding)

predictions.claim: NO POSITIONAL ORDER EFFECT: within batches, the acceptance rate of claims presented in the first half of a batch differs from the second half by <= 0.15 (the whitened order plus batching does not leak into the verdicts).
predictions.falsified_if: |first-half rate - second-half rate| > 0.15 (order effects present; the whitened-order guard would need strengthening before any rate in this run is trusted)

predictions.claim: 41-E JUDGE PARSE HOLDS ON THE LIVE ENVELOPES: (a) the measured envelope (built from the live run's T_unsigned/T_signed) parses with ALL THREE slots keyed by the REAL extractJudgeAnswers; (b) the adversarial wave-41-shape envelope parses with all three slots labeled holes and the stray 0.9 never leaking.
predictions.falsified_if: any hole in the measured parse, or any leaked value in the adversarial parse

honest_limits_registered_upfront: Single model (deepseek-reasoner), single prompt, single run, no sampling controls (API defaults); results are a seat probe with N=96, not a distribution over models or framings.
The strict seat's ground truth is the 44-a labels; the strict seat re-derivation inherits 44-a's known honest defects (2 should-PASS crowns rejected on their crown claim — recorded, unpatched).
Duplicate sources are visible to the model (4 distinct bodies across 96 claims); whether it uses that signal is measured (duplicate_visibility receipt + reason taxonomy), not controlled.
claim ids travel with items and correlate with breeding order (001..096); the model could in principle read age into ids. Whitening shuffles position, not ids. Disclosed.
Budget reality: ~10 calls means each call judges ~10 claims; batch-level context could induce correlation within a batch (measured via P5's position guard and the per-call receipt).
The gifted deepseek key is spent ONLY here, <= 10 calls, max_tokens <= 2000/call, usage receipted per call; no other lane's budget is touched.
